title: Naturality of recursively assembled independent input shifts
statement: For any interpretation d of independently labelled expressions in categories with integer shift, and natural primitive shift comparisons a, the recursively defined independent-slot comparison is natural in every input-family morphism. For the input-shift functor S_i(r), expression evaluation F, and endpoint-corrected comparison sigma_K: F(S_i(r)K) ≅ F(K)[r], one has F(S_i(r)f) ≫ sigma_N.hom = sigma_K.hom ≫ (F(f))[r]. The comparison sigma is the existing explicit unique-occurrence context construction of [def-pur-integral-expression-occurrences], with its equality endpoint identifications. The tensor-slot endofunctors are those of [def-pur-integral-tensor-shift-properties].

source.place: Step 2, canonical maps and integer shifts in independent expression inputs.

proof.text: Follow the selected occurrence. Variables give identity shifts. At unary vertices apply the operation functor to the induction square, then use its primitive shift naturality. At a tensor vertex injectivity of occurrence labels excludes the selected index from the other subtree; its evaluation therefore ignores the single-coordinate shift. Apply naturality of the designated left or right tensor isomorphism to the pair of actual evaluated maps. Equality transport along the explicit endpoint evaluation identities gives the asserted square.

theorem IndependentExpression.shift_naturality_generic
    {B : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} {X : I → Over B}
    {C : Scheme.{u} → Type v} [∀ W, Category.{w} (C W)] [∀ W, HasShift (C W) ℤ]
    (d : Interpretation C) (a : InterpretationShifts d) {W : Over B}
    (e : IndependentExpression B I X W) (K N : ∀ i, C (X i).left)
    (f : K ⟶ N) (i : I) (r : ℤ) :
    (e.val.evaluate d).map ((inputShift _ i r).map f) ≫
        ((e.val.evaluate d).mapIso (eqToIso (inputShift_obj _ N i r)) ≪≫
          e.shift d a N i r).hom =
      ((e.val.evaluate d).mapIso (eqToIso (inputShift_obj _ K i r)) ≪≫
          e.shift d a K i r).hom ≫ ((e.val.evaluate d).map f)⟦r⟧'
